5. TOOL TYPES AND OPTIONS
=========================

The same options work as tool types of the program's icon (select the icon,
then Information from the Icons menu) and as Shell arguments. A tool type
in parentheses, such as (LANG=en), is switched off; remove the parentheses
to use it. The icon comes with every option at its default.

  LANG=en | pl | ja
      Language of the text. Default: en. LANG=pl plays the Polish
      translation. LANG=ja plays the original Japanese text; no Japanese
      system software is needed, the game brings its own font.

  MODE=<screen mode id>
      The screen mode, as a hexadecimal mode id. Default: 0x8004, PAL
      HiRes Laced. Any mode that can show 640x400 works. 0x19004 is NTSC
      HiRes Laced. On a graphics card, the simplest way is to keep the
      default and let Picasso96 promote it to a card mode.

  AUDIO=paula | ahi | none
      Sound output. Default: paula. "ahi" plays through ahi.device,
      "none" plays silently.

  AHIUNIT=<n>
      The AHI unit to use with AUDIO=ahi. Default: 0.

  RATE=<Hz>
      The sample rate of the music and sound. Default: 11025. 22050
      sounds better but needs a faster processor than a 68040 at
      25 MHz, which plays it with gaps.

  AUDIOCPU=<percent>
      How much of the processor the sound may use, from 10 to 100.
      Default: 75. If the sound needs more, short gaps of silence are
      inserted instead, so that the game and the Workbench stay
      responsive. Raise it on a fast machine if you hear gaps.

  AUDIOBUF=<samples>
      Size of each sound buffer. Default: 1024 at 11025 Hz, 2048 at
      22050 Hz, about a tenth of a second. Larger buffers survive
      disk activity better but delay sound effects.

  PAULA14
      Plays Paula in 14-bit mode on all four channels for less noise.
      Default: off (8-bit on two channels). The voices then have no
      channels of their own: the game mixes them into the music, at the
      music's rate.

  VOICEPAK=<file>
      Where the voice data is (section 3, "Voices"). Default:
      xenon_voice.pak in the program's drawer, or next to the PAK= file.
      The characters speak whenever this file is found.

  NOVOICE
      No voices, even when the voice data is there.

  VOICEVOLUME=<percent>
      Volume of the voices, 1 to 100. Default: 100.

  VOLUME=<percent>
      Volume of the music and the sound effects, 1 to 100. Default: 50
      while the voices play (the music would cover them), 100 without
      them.

  VOICESTRICT
      A click during a voice does not cut it short: the line waits until
      the voice has finished, as in the Windows version. Default: off (OK
      or a click cuts the voice; Cancel always does).

  VOICEMIX
      With AUDIO=ahi: the game mixes the voices into the music itself
      instead of playing them on a second AHI channel. Needed when the AHI
      unit is set to a single channel in the AHI preferences (the voices
      are silent otherwise). The voices then play at the music's rate.

  OPN=lite | lite2
      The FM sound emulation. Default: lite. lite2 renders the FM part
      at double rate for a cleaner sound and needs about 1.6 times the
      processor time; for a 68060.

  WINDOW
      Play in a window on the Workbench instead of on the game's own
      screen. Default: off. The Workbench needs 256 colours or a graphics
      card (16 free colours for the game) and room for 640x400 pixels; on
      a native 640-pixel-wide Workbench the window has no border. If the
      Workbench cannot take the window, the game opens its own screen as
      usual. In a window F10 changes its size (section 4). On a 68040
      the game's own screen is faster: a window redraws more, and on a
      true colour Workbench fades show fewer steps.

  PUBSCREEN=<name>
      With WINDOW: the public screen to open the window on. Default: the
      default public screen, normally the Workbench.

  SCALE=1 | 2 | 3 | auto
      Show each pixel of the game 1, 2 or 3 times as large. Default: 1.
      "auto" takes the largest that fits. On the game's own screen this
      needs a graphics card: the game picks a card mode large enough
      (MODE= insists on one mode). Larger pictures cost more time; on a
      68040 keep 1.

  ASPECT
      Show the picture with the proportions of the PC-98's 4:3 monitor,
      by repeating every fifth line (640x400 becomes 640x480). Default:
      off. On the native PAL HiRes Laced screen it costs about a fifth
      more drawing; NTSC HiRes Laced (MODE=0x19004) already has these
      proportions.

  PRELOAD=auto | yes | no
      Load all game data into memory at start-up. Default: auto, which
      preloads when the data fits in fast RAM with 1.5 MB to spare.
      "yes" preloads whenever it fits, "no" never preloads.

  PAK=<file>
      Where the data file is. Default: xenon.pak in the program's drawer.

  QUIET
      No messages in the Shell window.

The program also understands AUTOPLAY, MAXTICKS, FAST, SNAPDIR and
PRESENTTEST. They exist for automated testing and are of no use for
playing.
